text:
maria-chen: Quick triage thread — ran nsys on the long-seq (8k) inference job against the 'llama-variant' build on dedicated-gpu. Timeline shows one small attention kernel firing extremely frequently and taking ~64% of GPU time but with low SM occupancy. perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/trace/abc123

jonathan: can you paste the kernel summary? low occupancy + high time usually hints at lots of tiny launches or heavy serial work inside the kernel.

maria-chen: paste from nsys report (abridged):
```
Kernel Name                        Calls   Total Time (ms)   Avg (ms)   SMs Active
attn_forward_small_seq             1240    512.3             0.413       12%
matmul_large                       62      89.6              1.445       78%
kv_prefetch                        360     34.2              0.095       22%
```

alex_k: hmm. attn_forward_small_seq avg 0.4ms, many calls. Could be per-token kernel (no batching) or we have sequence-split path launching per-layer per-token. Did you run with batching enabled?

maria-chen: this was with batching=auto (workload is mixed), but the trace shows many single-token micro-batches. Also KV cache hit ratio dropped to ~67% on this run (weird) — maybe cache sharding?

jonathan: @alex_k any chance the kernel selection heuristic is choosing a 'scalar-attn' variant for this seq length? We added a short-seq fallback that trades occupancy for simpler memory access and it could bite in long rolling windows.

alex_k: possible. Two quick checks: run nsys with --capture-range=cpu(0,100) to focus on the hot interval and capture launch params, and enable env VERBOSE_KERNEL_SELECT=1 to dump which variant is picked per-run.

maria-chen: ran the verbose dump, snippet:
```
[kernel_select] layer=4 seq=128 variant=attn_scalar fallback_reason=kv_miss
[kernel_select] layer=4 seq=512 variant=attn_blocked
[launch] attn_scalar grid=(128,1,1) block=(64,1,1)
```

perfbot: <automated> Suggestion: compare batch_size=1 vs batch_size=8; also run with KV_PREFETCH=on and measure stall_cyc from nsys metrics.

maria-chen: did batch=8 run; calls dropped from 1240 -> 210 and total attn time 512.3 -> 467.9ms (so per-call increased a bit but overall same %) — so batching helps somewhat but still disproportionate. KV hit improved to 91% with prefetch on and attn time dropped 18%.

jonathan: that indicates two factors: (1) selector chooses scalar variant when KV miss rate high, (2) prefetch helps reduce misses and lets selector pick higher-occupancy variant. We should add a policy to prefer blocked-attn if estimated KV hit > 0.8.

alex_k: agree. Also looking at SM util timeline in perfetto: long gaps between kernel launches with CPU-side dispatching. Could be overhead from per-layer CPU serialization. We should test fused-launch path (launch multiple layers in one kernel) to amortize CPU dispatch.

maria-chen: i ran a short perfetto capture with fused-launch toggled: fused path reduced kernel launches by ~44% and lowered total attn kernel time by ~23% in that segment. Attn occupancy for fused kernel is ~46%.

tracebot: <note> captured GPU metrics: issue_time_slices show high launch overhead spikes at 2.3s and 2.9s correlating with request boundary.

jonathan: next action items:
- alex_k: add a selector rule to prefer blocked-attn when KV_estimated_hit > 0.8 and batch_size>4.
- perf infra: expose KV hit estimate in the decision logs (trace friendly).
- maria-chen: gather 3 more traces across different model sizes and queue patterns. include batch=1,4,8 and KV_PREFETCH on/off.

maria-chen: will do. adding a short perf note to PR: we should avoid scalar-attn fallback when prefetch is on and KV hits above threshold.

alex_k: one more micro-observation: the scalar variant uses shared memory for small seq loops with divergent branches — that's why occupancy is low. If we switch to a vectorized blocked kernel by default when vectorization cost < 1.2x we should win overall. I'll prototype threshold-based selection and push a patch to the kernel repo.

maria-chen: thanks — i'll attach the 3 traces to the ticket. For now marking this thread resolved until we have selector logs + extra traces. :white_check_mark:

jonathan: awesome, thanks all :shipit:
